name: Ableton - Operator FM bass
description: Reference checklist for a heavy Ableton Operator bass: multiband control, drawn harmonics, filter distortion, velocity and LFO modulation, FM algorithms, Auto Filter and resampling. Not executable.

manual.instruction: Start with an Operator bass note. Put Multiband Dynamics before it and roll off the sub so the synth does not fight the dedicated sub or kick.
manual.verify: The bass has midrange weight without a bloated low end.
manual.why: dnksaus starts with multiband compression and turns off the sub band before designing the bass.

manual.instruction: Draw random harmonics in the oscillator until the waveform looks interesting. Shape it with Operator's filter distortion, then map velocity to filter frequency.
manual.verify: Harder notes open the filter and the bass responds to playing strength.
manual.why: dnksaus draws harmonics, uses filter distortion and assigns velocity to filter frequency.

manual.instruction: Use Operator's envelope and LFO on pitch, volume or filter. Try different FM algorithms and oscillator waveforms; the algorithm changes how the operators feed each other.
manual.verify: The patch has controlled movement and a different FM character than the starting tone.
manual.why: dnksaus demonstrates Operator's LFO, envelopes and FM algorithm menu.

manual.instruction: Add more filtering after the synth: an Auto Filter in band-pass, mapped to a macro, can turn the bass into a moving fill or a narrower variant.
manual.verify: The same patch can serve as a full bass and a filtered fill.
manual.why: dnksaus maps Auto Filter band-pass to a macro after the Operator patch.

manual.instruction: Print the result to an audio track and resample it. Modulate and chop the audio rather than keeping every layer live.
manual.verify: The resampled bass keeps its character and is easier to arrange.
manual.why: dnksaus resamples the Operator bass to an audio track and continues processing there.

notes: Source: dnksaus, 'Make HEAVY Dubstep Basses with Operator' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PFmBcZujMwk). Transcript summary, not quotes. Reference-only because the engine cannot create or verify Operator patches.
